title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study the outer/Galois action, by an element u (an element of Gal(Qbar/Q), or more generally an automorphism of 'Teichmüller type'), on a profinite fundamental groupoid of the sphere minus three points, P^1 - {0,1,∞}. Here \hat Π_{0,3} is the profinite free group on the loops ℓ_0, ℓ_1. The groupoid is taken at several base points that are distinguished by the symmetric group 𝔊_3 = S_3 acting on the three punctures:
- P^ω, P^{ω'}: the two fixed points of the order-3 rotation ρ, i.e. the points e^{±iπ/3}. These correspond to j = 0, which explains the notation ω, ω' = ω̄.
- R_i (i = 1, 2, 3): points fixed by the involutions, e.g. −1, 1/2, 2 on the real 'equator'. These correspond to j = 1728.
- Q_{ωi}: base points attached to the cusps, apparently tangential (next page: 'ici invisibles').
σ_∞ is the involution fixing ∞ and swapping 0 and 1; τ, τ_∞ denote the antiholomorphic reflection (complex conjugation), which swaps the hemispheres ω ↔ ω'.

Result of the previous page (62). The automorphisms of the groupoid VI_3 that are the identity on vertices and compatible with the S_3 action are parametrised by triples (λ, η, ξ') ∈ \hat Π_{0,3}^3 subject to one relation, the tentative 'relation des tresses'.

This page.
- (63) restates that relation in boxed form: β' = α' σ_∞(λ), where α' = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1} and β' = η σ_∞(η)^{-1}. When λ = ℓ_0^γ, i.e. λ is the image of the inertia loop at 0, then σ_∞(λ) = ℓ_1^γ. Written out, this is a 'cocycle' equation: η σ_∞(η)^{-1} = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1} · σ_∞(λ).
- Left margin: Grothendieck records how the parameters transform under the reflection τ: η ↦ τ_∞(η), ξ ↦ σ_∞τ_∞(ξ), and λ ↦ something like ε_0^{-1}(τ_∞(λ^{-1})). This gives the effect of conjugating u by complex conjugation.
- Right margin: a note on the inverse substitution (how α', β' and ξ, η transform), partly illegible.

Interpretation. The primed quantities were first introduced 'par le pur calcul' because they made the formulas of Th°3 nicest. Grothendieck now gives them a geometric meaning:
- (64) reversing the paths gives b'^ω_i = (b^ω_i)^{-1} = b^{ω'}_i, b̃'^ω_i = (b̃^ω_i)^{-1}, ã'^ω_i = (ã^ω_i)^{-1}.
- (65) under u these transform as u(b') = φ_{ωi}(β') b', u(b̃') = φ_{ωi}(α') b̃', u(ã') = ã' ψ_{ωi}(α̃'). Here φ_{ωi} and ψ_{ωi} transport an element of \hat Π_{0,3} to the local fundamental group at the relevant endpoint.
- (66) ξ' = ηξ is the Galois 'cocycle' of a composite path d̃^ω_i = c^ω_{ωi} · d^ω_{ωi} : P^ω → Q_{ωi} → R^{ω'}_i, from the order-3 point to the order-2 point through a cusp base point. The formula u(d̃) = φ(ξ') d̃ itself appears on the next page as (67).

Purpose. This is a hands-on description of the Galois (or GT-type) action on a fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4} with base points at the elliptic points of the quotient M_{0,4}/S_3 (the j-line). It is a step toward isolating the relations (the 2-cycle, 3-cycle and braid-type relations) that such automorphisms satisfy. This is the kind of relations later packaged as \hat{GT}.
errors: Apparent inconsistency in exponent: the transcription reads α' = ξ' ρ^{-1}(ξ')^{-1}, but the derivation on the previous page gives α' = ηξ ρ(ξ^{-1}η^{-1}) = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}. In the image the superscript on ρ is blotted out, i.e. a deleted '-1', so the correct reading is ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}. This is not an error by Grothendieck.
The relation in (62) is flagged with a question mark ('satisfaisant la relation des tresses ?'). Whether this single relation characterises all such groupoid automorphisms is not proved on this page.
The marginal transformation rule for λ under τ, ε_0^{-1}(τ_∞(λ^{-1})), is only partly legible and is not verified here.

ideas.what: Parametrising S_3-compatible automorphisms of the profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1-{0,1,∞}, based at the elliptic fixed points of S_3 and at cusp base points, by triples (λ, η, ξ') satisfying a twisted-cocycle relation η σ_∞(η)^{-1} = ξ'ρ(ξ')^{-1}σ_∞(λ)
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT action on fundamental groupoids with several base points; 2- and 3-cycle relations of \hat{GT} via symmetries
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990-91) for GT; Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura for groupoid/base-point refinements
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and base-point choices but gives no such explicit formulas

ideas.what: Using base points at the non-rational elliptic points e^{±iπ/3} (j=0) and at the order-2 points (j=1728), together with cusp base points, and tracking complex conjugation τ swapping them
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on étale paths to CM/orbifold points of the j-line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Wojtkowiak and others (1990s) for paths to non-tangential points

ideas.what: Geometric reinterpretation of computational parameters as Galois cocycles of reversed paths and of composite paths through a cusp base point (formulas 64-66)
ideas.modern_name: path-torsor cocycles / composition of étale paths

missed.claim: This is an early (≥1978, pre-Drinfeld) explicit treatment of the Galois action on the groupoid of M_{0,4} based at the S_3-elliptic points (j=0, j=1728), with the reflection τ included. Here the GT-type relations emerge as cocycle conditions for paths between orbifold points of the j-line. This links the genus-0 Teichmüller action to the arithmetic of M_{1,1}/SL_2(Z)-type orbifold points, a viewpoint the later GT literature mainly develops via tangential base points only.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Using actual elliptic points as base points could give alternative derivations of the 2- and 3-cycle relations of \hat{GT}. It could also give explicit Galois cocycles for paths to j=0 and j=1728, relevant to work on the Galois action on π_1 of M_{1,1} and on periods at CM points.

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether the triples satisfying the 'relation des tresses' exhaust the vertex-fixing, S_3-compatible automorphisms of VI_3. The question is left open here.
missed.quote: correspondent aux (λ, η, ξ') ... satisfaisant la relation des tresses ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This amounts to a presentation of an \hat{GT}-like group as automorphisms of a multi-based groupoid with orbifold base points; to my knowledge such a characterisation is not made explicit in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical step: it restates a relation and gives a geometric interpretation of the parameters. Its interest is the date and the choice of non-tangential, S_3-elliptic base points with τ-equivariance, which anticipates GT-type relations before Drinfeld and Ihara. The underlying mathematics, however, is now standard in spirit.
transcription_corrections: (63) second line: the superscript on ρ appears crossed out/blotted, so read α' = ξ' ρ(ξ')^{-1}, consistent with the previous page.
The interlinear insertion 'ce qui revient à β', γ', α̃'' should probably read '(ce qui revient à β', α', α̃')'.
Left margin probably begins 'τ(ω) : le procédé de [...] direct [...]' describing the action of τ on λ, η, ξ; the line ξ ↦ σ_∞τ_∞(ξ) is legible.
